title: Feature Engineering & Selection
html:
Feature engineering creates inputs that make the pattern easier to learn; feature selection removes inputs that add noise, cost or leakage. On tabular data, good features usually beat a fancier algorithm.

Engineering ideas

IdeaExample
Ratios & differencesprice_per_item = total / items, debt_to_income
Aggregates over historyPurchases in the last 7 / 30 days, average basket size per user
Date & time partsHour, weekday, month, is_weekend, days since signup
Cyclical encodingsin(2π·hour/24), cos(2π·hour/24) so 23:00 is next to 00:00
BinningAge bands — can help linear models capture non-linear effects
Interactions & polynomialsarea × quality, x² for linear models (PolynomialFeatures)
TextLength, keyword flags, TF-IDF (see Data Science)
Domain knowledgeBMI from height and weight; distance from coordinates

Selecting features

FamilyHow it worksscikit-learnTrade-off
FilterScore each feature against the target, independently of any modelVarianceThreshold, SelectKBest(f_classif / chi2 / mutual_info_classif)Fast; misses interactions
WrapperSearch subsets by repeatedly training a modelRFE, RFECV, SequentialFeatureSelectorModel-aware; expensive, can overfit the selection
EmbeddedSelection happens during trainingL1 (Lasso) coefficients, tree importances via SelectFromModelCheap; tied to one model's view
Watch out

Feature selection is part of training. Selecting features on the full dataset and then cross-validating produces badly optimistic scores — the Data Leakage topic demonstrates a model scoring far above chance on pure noise this way. Put the selector inside the Pipeline.

Why bother selecting?

  • Fewer irrelevant features → less overfitting, especially with few rows (see Curse of Dimensionality in the k-NN topic).
  • Faster training and prediction; fewer data pipelines to maintain in production.
  • Easier explanations.
  • Removing features that are available in training but not at prediction time prevents leakage.
Filter vs wrapper vs embedded feature selection?

Filters score features with a statistic (correlation, ANOVA F, mutual information) without training the final model — fast but blind to interactions. Wrappers (RFE, forward/backward selection) train models on candidate subsets — accurate but expensive and prone to overfitting the selection. Embedded methods select during training — Lasso zeroes coefficients, trees rank features by importance.

How would you encode the hour of day?

As a categorical (one-hot, 24 columns) if each hour behaves differently, or cyclically with sin(2π·h/24) and cos(2π·h/24) so the model sees 23:00 and 00:00 as neighbours. Tree models can also use the raw hour directly, splitting it into ranges.
